title: Titan Diwali Film Honours 16,000 Karigars Who Craft India's Festive Jewellery
excerpt: 'Sukriya, Karigar' follows four artisans whose work becomes family milestones — and behind the film sits a decade of documented change in how Titan's jewellery karigars work.
body:
• Titan Company's Diwali film 'Sukriya, Karigar', made with Ogilvy, honours the more than 16,000 karigars (artisans) in its jewellery-making network, following four of them as they craft pieces for family milestones.
  • The workforce behind the film is documented beyond the campaign: Titan set up India's first Karigar Centre at Hosur, Tamil Nadu, in 2014, and an independent factory visit described its 11,990 sq ft workshop employing artisans from Rajasthan and northern India.
  • A Tanishq vendor's account in Bullion World describes what changed for karigars under Titan's 4P framework: ergonomic workstations instead of floor seating, mandatory ESIC and provident fund enrolment, salary accounts and cadmium- and cyanide-free processes.
  • For Diwali gold buyers: Titan says its supplier standards under the 4P framework are validated by third-party audits — a concrete question to ask any jeweller is who made the piece and under what audited standards.

Every gold piece bought this Diwali passed through someone's hands long before it reached a showroom. Titan Company has built its festive film around those hands. 'Sukriya, Karigar' — released on the company's YouTube channel — honours the more than 16,000 karigars associated with Titan's jewellery-making network, according to the company's announcement.

Conceptualised with Ogilvy, the film follows four karigars at work: one making a child's first pair of earrings, one a necklace for a bride's mother, one a ring meant to express love, and one a kada marking a new beginning. It then follows the finished pieces to the people who receive them.

"Our karigars bring years of experience, knowledge and extraordinary attention to detail to their work. Supporting them means creating conditions in which their craft and livelihoods can thrive."

— Sharad, Chief Manufacturing Officer, Jewellery, Titan Company Limited

The workshop behind the film

The artisan network the film celebrates has been documented independently of the campaign. Titan says it established India's first Karigar Centre in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, in 2014. A reporter who visited Titan's Hosur operations for Indulge Express described the Karigar Centre, a short drive from the main Tanishq factory, as an 11,990 square-foot space employing artisans from Rajasthan and other parts of northern India, in an almost corporate-like set-up far removed from the unhealthy and unhygienic conditions of the small-scale workshops common in gold jewellery towns.

What those traditional conditions cost artisans is spelled out by G. Ganesh, proprietor of Vasantham Creations, a Tanishq vendor at Hosur, writing in Bullion World. Karigars traditionally sat on the floor, hunched over low worktables, with lights positioned extremely close to see fine work. Over time, he wrote, many developed chronic back pain and vision problems, especially after the age of 40.

What changed at the workbench

According to Ganesh's account, the response was to redesign the workspace: ergonomic tables with tools within easy reach, so karigars could work seated in proper chairs. The changes extended beyond furniture. Many karigars were unaware of benefits such as ESIC health insurance and the provident fund, or did not know how to access them, so enrolment was made mandatory. His firm provides every artisan a dedicated salary account under a zero-cash wage policy, trains artisans in fire safety, chemical handling and emergency evacuation, and maintains cadmium-free and cyanide-free processes.

These practices sit inside Titan's 4P framework — People, Place, Process and Planet. The framework has outside recognition: Tanishq and Mia by Tanishq received the Diamonds Do Good Purpose-Driven Business Leadership Award in Las Vegas in 2025, with The Retail Jeweller reporting that the brands' Titan Supplier Engagement Protocol applies the 4P framework and is validated by third-party audits, and that the brands have established artisan parks providing safe, pollution-free workspaces for karigars. Titan also says it introduced training programmes for women karigars last year, widening participation in a trade the company's own film presents as its foundation.

Why it matters to the person buying

Diwali is one of the year's biggest gold-buying seasons, and most buyers never learn anything about the person who made what they purchase. Titan's film is, on its face, a thank-you. But the verifiable structure behind it — a named artisan centre dating to 2014, supplier standards subject to third-party audit, and a vendor describing specific changes to seating, lighting, insurance enrolment and pay — gives buyers something more useful than sentiment: a set of questions worth putting to any jeweller, Titan or otherwise. Who made this piece, where, and under what audited standards? On the evidence published so far, Titan is one of the few large Indian jewellers answering those questions in public.
